intro.title: Copy List with Random Pointer
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that creates a deep copy of a linked list where each node has a 'next' pointer and a 'random' pointer. You will learn how to traverse a linked list and use a hash map to store mappings between original and copied nodes to efficiently handle the random pointers. The main technologies involved are JavaScript objects, the Map data structure, and pointer manipulation. This exercise will help you understand linked list operations and the importance of reference handling in algorithms.
intro.usecase: This pattern appears in complex UI systems where components have relationships beyond simple parent-child hierarchies, such as interactive diagram editors where nodes have both structural connections and cross-references. For example, in a project management dashboard, task cards might display both their direct dependencies (next pointers) and related tasks from different project branches (random pointers). Developers encounter this when cloning DOM elements with event listeners that reference other elements, or when serializing component trees in state management libraries where components have references to unrelated peers. Understanding this algorithm helps when implementing undo/redo systems, collaborative editing features, or any scenario requiring deep copying of interconnected objects while preserving complex relationships.
